# 67js

> A 3D engine that AI agents drive. Real-time WebGL2 scenes in the browser, and deterministic PNG, MP4 and GLB output from the same scene.

67js has an MCP server (`67js-mcp`, 24 tools) that builds, edits, looks at and renders scenes from JSON recipes.
The same engine is a JavaScript library for pages and Node. The library API is in the guide below.
Scenes are plain data with stable IDs, so an agent can edit by ID and check each change with a rendered image.

## Connect

- npm package: `@codepawlhq/67js`. The MCP server is its `67js-mcp` binary. Node.js 20.19 or newer and an installed Chrome are required.
- Claude Code plugin, which adds the server and both skills: `/plugin marketplace add codepawl/67.js`, then `/plugin install 67js@67js`.
- Any other MCP client: `npm install 67js@npm:@codepawlhq/67js`, then run Node on `node_modules/67js/bin/67js-mcp.mjs --backend gpu --memory 192` over stdio. Use the absolute path.
- Setup, flags and client notes: [mcp.md](https://67js.codepawl.com/mcp.md).
- Skills in the package: `skills/build-67js-scene` (build and light) and `skills/render-67js-media` (stills and video).

## Start

1. Call `scene_capabilities`. It reports the recipe fields, limits and budgets, and it is the source for field detail.
2. Create a scene, call `scene_inspect` for IDs and the revision, edit in small batches, and call `scene_look` after each batch.
3. Checkpoint before a risky change. Restore it if the picture is worse. Call `scene_dispose` when finished.

## To do X, call Y

- Create a scene: `scene_capabilities`, then `scene_create` with a JSON recipe, or `scene_asset_catalog` and `scene_create_asset` for a GLB. [Docs](https://67js.codepawl.com/agent-scene.md)
- Edit parts, transforms and the camera: `scene_inspect` for stable IDs and the revision, then `scene_apply` with `expectedRevision`. [Docs](https://67js.codepawl.com/agent-scene.md)
- Shape geometry: `mesh_inspect`, `mesh_edit`, `mesh_stack`. [Docs](https://67js.codepawl.com/mesh.md)
- Materials, looks, HDRI, fog, effects: `scene_apply` with `set-material`, `set-environment`, `set-effects`, `set-shadow`; `scene_asset_catalog` lists HDRI and look IDs. [Docs](https://67js.codepawl.com/agent-look.md)
- Lights and shadows: `scene_apply` with `set-environment` (sun, sky, point lights) and `set-shadow`. [Docs](https://67js.codepawl.com/lighting.md)
- Camera and lens: `scene_apply` with `set-camera`; check the framing with `scene_look` or `scene_review`. [Docs](https://67js.codepawl.com/camera-path.md)
- Animation: `scene_apply` with `set-motion`; preview with `scene_look` and `motionTime`. [Docs](https://67js.codepawl.com/agent-motion.md)
- Imported character motion: `scene_inspect` with `kind: hierarchy`, then `scene_apply` with `set-asset-node`. [Docs](https://67js.codepawl.com/agent-character-motion.md)
- Bake light: Put `bakes` in the recipe; `scene_capabilities` lists the fields. [Docs](https://67js.codepawl.com/light-bake.md)
- Review the result: `scene_look` for one PNG, `scene_review` for a labeled grid of up to four views. [Docs](https://67js.codepawl.com/agent-review.md)
- Render a still or a video: `scene_render_submit`, poll `scene_render_status`, read `scene_render_result`, then `scene_render_release`. [Docs](https://67js.codepawl.com/agent-render-jobs.md)
- Export a model: `scene_export_glb`, or `scene_export_recipe` for the JSON recipe. [Docs](https://67js.codepawl.com/export-glb.md)
- Make a playable game: `scene_apply` with `set-game` (topic `game` in `scene_capabilities`), then `scene_export_web` for a static folder. [Docs](https://67js.codepawl.com/game.md)
- Recover from an error: `scene_restore` to a `scene_checkpoint`, or `scene_inspect` for the current revision and retry; every error names its next step. [Docs](https://67js.codepawl.com/mcp.md)

## All tools

- `scene_capabilities`: Index of supported recipe features and runtime budgets; pass topic for the detail of one.
- `scene_create`: Create a render scene from a JSON recipe; the result has its sessionId.
- `scene_asset_catalog`: List content-bound GLB and PNG, JPEG or WebP image IDs from the configured local asset directory.
- `scene_create_asset`: Create the active scene from a catalog GLB and editable asset recipe.
- `scene_inspect`: Read revision, counts and selected nodes.
- `scene_walkmap`: Walkable map on a grid: rows of . walkable, x blocked, # no surface.
- `mesh_inspect`: Check recipe geometries as polygon meshes: vertex, edge and face counts, triangles/quads/n-gons, connected and closed parts, face tags...
- `mesh_edit`: Append edits to a recipe mesh geometry or an imported asset part such as mesh-0 (or replace its edit log), atomically like scene_apply:...
- `mesh_stack`: Set the non-destructive modifier stack of a recipe mesh geometry (ops and fields: scene_capabilities meshModifiers), evaluated after its...
- `scene_apply`: Atomically edit transforms, look, camera or materials.
- `scene_look`: Render the active scene as a bounded PNG, optionally with part labels.
- `scene_review`: Compare one to four independent camera or motion samples in one labeled PNG grid.
- `scene_checkpoint`: Save a private recipe snapshot.
- `scene_restore`: Restore a checkpoint atomically using the current revision.
- `scene_release_checkpoint`: Release one checkpoint slot.
- `scene_export_recipe`: Read a detached canonical JSON recipe for reproduction.
- `scene_export_glb`: Write the active scene as a GLB file in the configured jobs folder, under a server-chosen name (the result has the path, byte count and...
- `scene_export_web`: Write the scene with its game as a static web build in the jobs folder: index.html, game.json and engine/, which any static host serves...
- `scene_dispose`: Dispose the active scene and its checkpoints, releasing renderer resources.
- `scene_render_submit`: Start one asynchronous snapshot job in the configured private job store.
- `scene_render_status`: Read render job state and durable frame progress.
- `scene_render_cancel`: Request cancellation of one job.
- `scene_render_result`: Read completed local output paths, MIME types, byte counts, SHA-256 digests and measured render metrics.
- `scene_render_release`: Delete the owned files and record for a terminal job, freeing store quota.

Call `scene_capabilities` for field detail. This list is generated from the server's tool registry by `scripts/generate-llms.mjs`.

## Docs

- [Complete plain-text guide](https://67js.codepawl.com/guide.md): renderer, parts, materials, cameras, animation, export and troubleshooting.
- [MCP server](https://67js.codepawl.com/mcp.md), [scene recipes](https://67js.codepawl.com/agent-scene.md), [look and lighting](https://67js.codepawl.com/agent-look.md), [motion](https://67js.codepawl.com/agent-motion.md), [review](https://67js.codepawl.com/agent-review.md), [render jobs](https://67js.codepawl.com/agent-render-jobs.md), [imported assets](https://67js.codepawl.com/agent-asset.md).
- [GLB contract](https://67js.codepawl.com/gltf.md): supported assets and conversion limits.
- [Release metadata](https://67js.codepawl.com/release.json): package name, version, install command and commit.
- [Changelog data](https://67js.codepawl.com/changelog.json): every release and the unreleased changes with issue numbers and breaking flags. Read it before relying on a feature the docs describe.
